key_facts: July 9 update (NMC 18:00 CST Orange Warning, Xinhua/State Flood Control HQ 19:29 CST Level III upgrade for Zhejiang & Fujian, CMA press briefing 19:07 CST via 21jingji, Chinanews/jwview 20:55 CST, Haixia/hxnews 22:25 CST, Fuzhou News 10:06 CST): At 17:00 CST July 9, Super Typhoon Bavi (16-level, 52 m/s, 935 hPa; 7-level gale radius 500 km, 10-level 280-300 km) was at 18.7N, 128.9E (~1,030 km SE of Keelung), moving NW at 15-20 km/h toward NE Taiwan for July 11 daytime hit/graze and July 11 evening mainland landfall along Fuqing, Fujian to Wenling, Zhejiang (13-15 level, 40-48 m/s), with Fujian Met/Fuzhou News pinpointing Lianjiang, Fujian to Cangnan, Zhejiang as most likely. Two opposing evacuation forces roughly balance in Zhejiang's favor: (1) Pro-Zhejiang: CMA Chief Forecaster Xiang Chunyi warned July 9 that Bavi's dangerous right-front semicircle (右侧) hits Zhejiang/Yangtze Delta hardest with heavier moisture flux, stronger winds, and storm surge; Zhejiang Met forecasts 30+ hours of 10-level+ gales (vs 20h in central-north Fujian). Zhejiang already evacuated >11,000+ people by July 9 morning (Shengsi 9,000+ tourists, Wenzhou Nanji/Beiji islands 2,000+, earlier remote islands >3,000) and recalled all 4,269 Zhoushan vessels; historically Zhejiang also out-evacuates Fujian even on northern Fujian landfalls (2013 Fitow Fuding: ZJ 574k vs FJ 177k; 2018 Maria Lianjiang: ZJ 390k vs FJ 240k; 2024 Gaemi Putian: ZJ 287k vs FJ 290k). (2) Pro-Fujian: Landfall centerline favors northern Fujian (Lianjiang-Fuding), and Fujian Maritime upgraded early to Level II at 20:00 CST July 9 halting all 57 ferry routes north of Xiamen, 110 marine projects, 14 wind farms, and 273 construction ships. Zhejiang edged to 0.57 (from 0.55), Fujian 0.40, Shanghai trimmed 0.02->0.01, Jiangsu 0.01, Guangdong 0.01 (sum 1.00).
next_review_trigger: FINAL DAY check July 10 for official provincial cumulative evacuation figures from Zhejiang and Fujian Emergency Management/Flood Control HQs.
